at: (English version) to the Commission Cornelia Ernst (The Left) (25 April 2024) Subject: Frontex in Albania 1.
Is the Commission aware of reports and evidence of pushbacks from Albania to Greece?
If so, what is the Commission’s experience of how Frontex deals with rights violations in its operational areas in Albania?

3. What concrete measures has the Commission taken, as part of its oversight role with respect to the Frontex Management Board, to ensure compliance with human rights obligations in Frontex’s operations in Albania? (20 June 2024) The Commission is not aware of any reports that suggest the involvement of staff of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) in expulsions from Albania to Greece. The Commission’s position remains that safe and effective border management must be firmly rooted in the respect for fundamental rights and international law, including the right to asylum and the principle of non-refoulement. The Commission is not directly involved in Frontex’s execution of its operational activities. Nevertheless, in its capacity as a Member of the Frontex Management Board, the Commission is committed to ensuring that the Agency protects and promotes fundamental rights in all its activities, and is equipped with the tools, framework and safeguards to do so. Today, Frontex has in place a robust system for accountability and compliance with fundamental rights, resting on pillars such as the work of its 46 fundamental rights monitors, which in 2023 performed 1 627 days of monitoring across all Frontex deployments and activities, and reporting systems such as the serious incident reporting mechanism and Frontex complaints mechanism.
